answer:
I've completed the research. Here's a summary of the key findings:

## Summary: Florida 2026 GOP Gubernatorial Primary Debates

**Important premise correction:** David Jolly is the **Democratic** frontrunner (a former GOP congressman who switched parties), not a Republican primary candidate. The GOP primary candidates are Byron Donalds, James Fishback, Jay Collins, and Paul Renner.

**Was there a GOP primary debate in summer 2026?**

1. **The party-sanctioned debate effectively did NOT happen.** The Republican Party of Florida imposed a strict "10/10/10" qualification rule (≥10% polling, ≥$10M raised, ≥10,000 donors). **Only Byron Donalds qualified**, so the June 27, 2026 "Sunshine State Showdown" (Seminole Hard Rock, Hollywood, FL) held no debate — just separate candidate appearances. Rivals and even Gov. DeSantis accused the RPOF of rigging the criteria to protect Donalds.

2. **One actual GOP debate WAS held — July 3, 2026** — an unsanctioned "undercard" titled *"The Future of Florida,"* hosted by podcaster Patrick Bet-David on YouTube (after no TV network would air it). **Jay Collins, James Fishback, and Paul Renner participated; Byron Donalds boycotted it** (he was mentioned 60+ times as "the elephant not in the room").

3. **Donalds has consistently refused** to debate his GOP rivals, calling their demands "stunts" and refusing to give "participation trophies." No debate including Donalds is scheduled before the **August 18, 2026** primary.

**Bonus context:** There's active litigation (Collins trying to remove Fishback from the ballot over residency, hearing starting July 21), and Donalds has challenged Democrat David Jolly to three *general-election* fall debates — though a proposed Oct. 15 FAU debate remains unconfirmed by both the RPOF and Jolly's campaign.

Full structured findings with 11 sources and 11 data points have been submitted.

key_facts: Florida's 2026 GOP gubernatorial primary is August 18, 2026; general election is November 3, 2026.
David Jolly is the DEMOCRATIC frontrunner (former Republican who switched parties), NOT a GOP primary candidate.
The Republican Party of Florida (RPOF) set '10/10/10' debate qualification criteria: >=10% polling, >=$10M raised, >=10,000 donors.
Only Byron Donalds met the RPOF 10/10/10 criteria, becoming the lone qualifier; no sanctioned debate took place.
The RPOF 'Sunshine State Showdown' was scheduled for June 27, 2026 at Seminole Hard Rock Hotel & Casino, Hollywood, FL — but held no debate, only separate candidate appearances.
An unsanctioned 'undercard' GOP debate WAS held July 3, 2026, hosted by podcaster Patrick Bet-David on YouTube (PBD Podcast).
The July 3 debate featured Jay Collins, James Fishback, and Paul Renner; Byron Donalds skipped it and was mentioned 60+ times.
Donalds has repeatedly refused to debate his GOP primary rivals, calling debate demands 'stunts' and refusing to give 'participation trophies.'
Jay Collins filed a legal challenge to remove James Fishback from the ballot over a 7-year residency requirement; a two-day court hearing was set to begin July 21, 2026.

Donalds challenged Democrat David Jolly to three general-election debates (reiterated ~July 20, 2026); a nonpartisan Oct 15, 2026 gubernatorial debate at FAU was announced but not confirmed/sanctioned by RPOF or Jolly.
